- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in recognizing momentum; shift forecast upward by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven periods; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.7 in last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model tends to misalign with true direction; favor 3-day moving average of sentiment to guide forecast direction.
